41925c3c7c666d94fae18d5aaf680ec9ed053201.description: Submit this worker attempt's report, summary and observed checks. A check that failed, was then fixed, and whose later identical rerun passed is `passed`: cite the passing rerun's tool_call_ref and describe the failure-then-fix history in the report. An identical rerun repeats the exact argv and cwd, either on the same operation and profile or across command_run and outside_command in either direction. An explicit supported command_correction can supersede a mistaken invocation with a same-name later passing correction of this attempt, never pass the original argv. Complete whole-worktree git diff --check failures confined to sibling writers' reserved paths are not attributable to this worker; the failed evidence remains visible. Scope diff/whitespace checks to owned paths. `assignment_outcome=failed` is reserved for when the delivered work itself does not reach the assignment's goal, never merely because an earlier attempt failed before being fixed. summary is a short plain-language paragraph -- what was done and the current state -- without internal jargon (runtime codes, route names, revisions, receipts) unless the user asked about them. report is required in every call, a review included, and is one plain string, never an object: the complete report Markdown (optionally titled with report_title), which the runtime publishes; or, after create_draft, draft_write and write_report, only that write_report's report_id. summary, verdict and findings never replace it. Decision-brief items (conclusion, evidence, checks, contradictions, limits, next action) are Markdown sections inside the report, never separate fields. If the engine reports that the call could not be parsed, nothing reached Cortex: resend the same arguments with valid serialization and the same request_key. Use checks=[] only if no automated command ran. Each checks item has name (a stable check name) and outcome (passed|failed|not_run|unverified; there is no status field). passed needs the tool_call_ref, cited by one check only, of a complete exit-0 command_run (or user-confirmed outside_command) of this attempt; failed cites its nonzero receipt; not_run or unverified needs a concrete blocker; command is an optional argv array of strings, descriptive only for passed or failed. Engine-native shell calls, report ids and project_git (context only) are never check receipts. Do not send closed_by; the runtime derives it. Use a fresh request_key for a new result; retry an uncertain call only with the identical key and payload. Reviewers must include verdict=APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or BLOCK; other workers omit verdict. An open failed check is otherwise refused with open_failed_check before recording or publishing (a reviewer with verdict=REQUEST_CHANGES may cite a failed check as its finding: that review is recorded as completed and starts a fix cycle), leaving the channel active; the refusal names the failed receipt, the relevant rerun and its evidence gap, and says when no exact rerun can close it. A failed receipt that any result_submit of this attempt already presented (even a refused one) must be cited again by every later submission, failed outcome included, or it is refused with omitted_failed_check. A mistake in your own bounded standalone python/python3 -c probe (a syntax error, one wrong regex literal or one wrong literal-data expectation) may instead be retracted with checks[].invocation_error bound to the corrected passing run: both receipts stay visible and the failure is retracted, not passed. Runtime verification and actual project test/lint/build failures are never retracted. A mistyped command line whose own output shows the check never started (usage, unrecognized-flag or file-not-found error for the command itself) is not a failed check: do not cite it; cite the corrected command's receipt and describe the mistyped run in the report. The receipt carries node_status (completed or failed), not task acceptance. Top-level write_report-only fields such as artifacts are ignored.

inputSchema.description: Structured fields; use the exact advertised properties.

assignment_outcome.description: Optional: send failed only to intentionally submit a failed assignment, when the delivered work itself does not reach the assignment's goal -- never merely because a check failed before being fixed. Otherwise an open failed check is refused with open_failed_check before recording or revoking the channel; rerun exactly the receipt argv at the same cwd (on the same operation, or across command_run and outside_command) and cite the later passed receipt. Never silently omit a real failed check (a mistyped command line that never started the check is not one; see checks[].outcome). Even with failed, every failed receipt an earlier result_submit of this attempt presented must be cited again, or the result is refused with omitted_failed_check.

checks.description: Declare planned automated checks early through check_preflight before work depends on them. A missing executable must be installed project-privately or replaced with an executable approach; if neither is possible, ask the owner immediately. Qualitative human-only judgements are separate manual items: report them with no command and a concrete blocker; Workspace labels them Check manually, never a pass/fail or acceptance blocker. Policy-prohibited checks remain explicitly not_run with their named policy, never failed or automatically executed. Automated command checks, up to 20; [] when no command ran and no check was blocked. Each item needs name and outcome (passed, failed, not_run, unverified). A passed check needs tool_call_ref copied from an exit-0 command_run or confirmed outside_command of this attempt; command argv alone never verifies it. A failed check may cite its nonzero receipt. not_run or unverified require a concrete blocker; command argv is retained only for these gap checks and may identify the exact blocked command. A supplied command on passed/failed is ignored as evidence; the runtime derives the command from the receipt. Do not send closed_by: the runtime calculates it. project_git is context only, not a check receipt: describe its status/diff observations in the report, never cite or invent a receipt from large_output_id. These are not qualitative review remarks: read files and inspected code belong in the report body, not checks.

items.description: Structured fields; use the exact advertised properties.

blocker.description: Required and non-whitespace for not_run and unverified; forbidden for passed and failed. State the concrete condition that prevented running or establishing this specific check: for example, a named unavailable host, or a documented project policy that requires an explicit owner request which was not given, such as "paid live check not requested by the owner". "Not run", "out of scope" or "not requested" alone is not a blocker.

command.description: Required: 1 to 128 items; [] is rejected. Optional literal argv. This command is retained only for not_run or unverified gap checks; it identifies the blocked command and lets a later verified identical run close the gap. For passed or failed, it is descriptive only: the runtime derives the actual command and pass/fail evidence exclusively from tool_call_ref, never from this array.

items.description: One literal argument of the command this check ran or would run.

command_correction.description: Optional explicit supersession of a failed invocation by a corrected command; retain both checks. Runtime derives superseded_by, never send it.

corrected_by.description: Exact tool_call_ref of the later verified passing correction, cited once with the same check name in this result and same attempt, operation, cwd and profile, with different argv. Never a runtime verification receipt.

reason.description: Explain the command mistake and correction. Eligible: supported standalone Python probe syntax/regex/literal-expectation corrections, or a direct Python script whose complete output contains only argparse usage and an unrecognized-arguments or missing-required-arguments startup error (exit 2), corrected without changing script/interpreter flags. Real project test/lint/build failures cannot be superseded by another argv. Both receipts stay visible; the failure stays failed history with runtime-derived superseded_by, current outcome superseded, never passed.

invocation_error.description: Optional explicit self-retraction on a failed check only. Bind a supported invocation error to a later passing correction and explain it; runtime validates both receipts and retains the failure, not a synthetic pass. Do not send retracted_by or closed_by.

corrected_by.description: Exact tool_call_ref of a later observed passing correction, cited once as a passed check with the same name in this result and same attempt, operation, cwd and profile; only the -c probe source may differ, and it must differ. Never a claimed, foreign, incomplete, trivial or runtime-owned verification receipt.

reason.description: Nonempty explanation of your own probe invocation mistake and its correction. Eligible only: a failed bounded standalone python/python3 -c probe (only -B, -I or -S before -c) with complete retained output that hit a source-backed SyntaxError; a regex/AssertionError over a literal re pattern; or an AssertionError in a literal-data probe (only single-assignment literal bindings and == asserts, with unary len/sorted/sum/min/max/all/any/abs) whose expectation is statically false. The correction changes exactly one regex pattern literal, or the one false expected literal so every assertion holds; nothing else may change. Runtime verification and actual project test/lint/build failures cannot be retracted. The failed outcome and receipt stay in history with runtime-derived retracted_by; current outcome is retracted, never passed. Other invocation errors retain the existing mistyped-command or exact-rerun path.

name.description: Specific stable name of this automated command check, e.g. "unit tests for services/trading" or "ruff on changed files". Reuse exactly the same name for a later passing rerun that closes this check; do not use a report title, task name, or qualitative review remark.

outcome.description: passed: you ran it in this attempt with command_run (or a user-confirmed outside_command) and it exited 0; requires tool_call_ref (see its evidence rule). failed: it ran and failed; always kept as failed, and result_submit refuses an open failure with open_failed_check unless assignment_outcome="failed" intentionally submits a failed assignment. A failure closes only when a later passed check of this same result cites a rerun of exactly the same command -- the same argv and cwd, on the same operation and profile or across command_run and outside_command in either direction -- that is the latest such run in this attempt: then it stays as history with closed_by. Report a fixed failure that way, or cite only the passing rerun and describe the failure-then-fix history in the report, never by silently dropping it; a different argv needs an explicit supported command_correction (superseded history, never a pass of the original argv). A direct whole-worktree git diff --check whose complete whitespace diagnostics name only sibling writers' reserved paths is runtime-attributed not_attributable, never passed; own writes, unknown paths and runtime verification remain failures. A supported mistake in your own bounded standalone Python probe (see invocation_error.reason) may instead be explicitly retracted with invocation_error; it remains failed history with retracted_by, never passed. A run whose own output shows the check never started because its command line was mistyped (a usage, unrecognized-flag or file-not-found error for the command itself) is not a failed check of the work: do not cite it as one; cite the receipt of the corrected command and describe the mistyped run in the report. Once any result_submit of this attempt cited a failed receipt, even a refused one, every later submission must cite it again (omitted_failed_check otherwise); relabelling it not_run or unverified does not count. A test, lint, type check or build that ran and reported failures is always a real failed check. not_run: a real blocker prevented running it. unverified: it ran but its result could not be established. not_run and unverified require blocker. A passed claim the runtime cannot verify is recorded as unverified with evidence_gap, or as failed when its cited command or a later run of the same command exited nonzero; the result receipt lists each such check.

probe_withdrawn.description: Optional, on a failed check only: why this was your own exploratory probe and not a check of the work -- a diagnostic call whose failure was expected (a 404 for a resource that should not exist) or a throwaway probe that asked the wrong question. It must cite its real nonzero receipt; it stays failed history, current outcome retracted, never passed, and reviewers see it with this reason. A project test, lint, type check or build that ran and failed is a real failed check and must never be withdrawn.

tool_call_ref.description: For a verified passed check, copy the exact tool_call_ref field from the completed command_run (or user-confirmed outside_command) result of this same attempt; engine shell calls never verify a check, and their exit code or output is not retained. project_git is context only and cannot verify checks. Never derive the receipt from a command, draft, report or engine shell call. A real gateway receipt has gateway: followed by 32 lowercase hex characters, but its shape alone proves nothing. Cite one receipt for one check only, after confirming complete=true, exit_code=0 and untruncated retained output. A missing, foreign, pending, failed, truncated, replayed or trivial receipt makes a claimed pass unverified or failed, not accepted as passed. Truncated means the retained output, never the 64 KiB inline part (output_truncated), so run a check command directly: a shell script that ends with exit $VARIABLE verifies only in the plain form CHECK; NAME=$?; print/read commands; exit $NAME (evidence_gap status_variable_unproven otherwise). A failed check may cite its nonzero command receipt; a later passing rerun of the same argv and cwd closes it and the runtime supplies closed_by in the result (do not send closed_by).

report.description: Required in every result_submit, a review included: this attempt's report as one plain string, never an object. Either the complete report Markdown, which the runtime publishes as this attempt's immutable report before recording the result: the opening decision brief (conclusion, observed evidence, checks, contradictions, limits, next action) as Markdown sections, then the detailed evidence, with no draft marker and no template placeholder comments. Or, after create_draft, draft_write and write_report, only the exact report_id that write_report returned to this worker in this attempt (r_ plus 12 lowercase hex characters, nothing else in the string). Never a draft_id, a tool_call_ref or a report of another attempt. summary, verdict and findings never replace it. Retry an uncertain delivery with exactly the same request_key and entire payload; a changed report needs a new logical delivery.

report_title.description: Optional, only with inline Markdown in report: readable English report title. Omit it to use the first Markdown heading of report (else its first line). Ignored when report is a report_id.

request_key.description: New unique key for this logical result_submit delivery, distinct from keys used for prior mutations on this channel. verification.description: Required: 1 to 16 items; [] is rejected. Corrected verification commands. Only after the runtime verification failed and the work itself is fine: it verifies again without redoing the reviewed work. When the code is wrong, submit a new plan instead. Runtime verification runs in one fixed sandbox in every access mode; project writes outside git-ignored directories are discarded when it ends (refused where the host cannot overlay), and no user consent, permission or mode change alters that sandbox, so never ask the user to authorize it. Required for every plan, including an investigation-only or trivial one: verification runs even when nothing changed. The runtime runs these commands once after review, each until it exits; this is where the project's whole documented suite belongs. Copy each command exactly from the project's documented verification (docs/project/verification.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Makefile or package.json scripts), interpreter included, e.g. [["python3","-B","-m","pytest","-q"]]. When the project documents no verification, send the smallest command that exits nonzero if the requested result is wrong, using only the project's files and standard tools, e.g. [["node","--check","src/app.js"]] for a script; for an investigation-only plan, one that checks the investigated files. A command that only prints, reads, lists or searches (echo, cat, ls, grep, rg, find, test, true, read-only git and the like) is refused, because its exit status does not prove the work. Each command is an argv array of literal strings: no shell operators, pipes, redirection or substitution; environment variables as ["env","NAME=value",...]. Availability is probed before accepting the plan. If a tool is missing, arrange project-private installation or another executable approach; if neither is possible, ask the owner immediately through the existing question route.

items.description: Required: 1 to 64 items; [] is rejected. One verification command as argv: literal string arguments, no shell.

Literal argument of a verification command, copied exactly from the project's own documented verification (docs/project/verification.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Makefile or package.json scripts) when it documents any, interpreter path included; set environment variables with ["env", "NAME=value", ...]. Runs as argv without a shell: do not use command substitution, backticks, redirection, pipes, shell operators or standalone parentheses. Runs with the owner's tools; only git-ignored paths are writable.

a19720b95eaa601d73dd2dab901cec0e146ad1c6.description: Submit this worker attempt's report, summary and observed checks. A check that failed, was then fixed, and whose later identical rerun passed is `passed`: cite the passing rerun's tool_call_ref and describe the failure-then-fix history in the report. An identical rerun repeats the exact argv and cwd, either on the same operation and profile or across command_run and outside_command in either direction. An explicit supported command_correction can supersede a mistaken invocation with a same-name later passing correction of this attempt, never pass the original argv. Complete whole-worktree git diff --check failures confined to sibling writers' reserved paths are not attributable to this worker; the failed evidence remains visible. Scope diff/whitespace checks to owned paths. `assignment_outcome=failed` is reserved for when the delivered work itself does not reach the assignment's goal, never merely because an earlier attempt failed before being fixed. summary is a short plain-language paragraph -- what was done and the current state -- without internal jargon (runtime codes, route names, revisions, receipts) unless the user asked about them. report is required in every call, a review included, and is one plain string, never an object: the complete report Markdown (optionally titled with report_title), which the runtime publishes; or, after create_draft, draft_write and write_report, only that write_report's report_id. summary, verdict and findings never replace it. Decision-brief items (conclusion, evidence, checks, contradictions, limits, next action) are Markdown sections inside the report, never separate fields. If the engine reports that the call could not be parsed, nothing reached Cortex: resend the same arguments with valid serialization and the same request_key. Use checks=[] only if no automated command ran. Each checks item has name (a stable check name) and outcome (passed|failed|not_run|unverified; there is no status field). passed needs the tool_call_ref, cited by one check only, of a complete exit-0 command_run (or user-confirmed outside_command) of this attempt; failed cites its nonzero receipt; not_run or unverified needs a concrete blocker; command is an optional argv array of strings, descriptive only for passed or failed. Engine-native shell calls, report ids and project_git (context only) are never check receipts. Do not send closed_by; the runtime derives it. Use a fresh request_key for a new result; retry an uncertain call only with the identical key and payload. Reviewers must include verdict=APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or BLOCK; other workers omit verdict. An open failed check is otherwise refused with open_failed_check before recording or publishing (a reviewer with verdict=REQUEST_CHANGES may cite a failed check as its finding: that review is recorded as completed and starts a fix cycle), leaving the channel active; the refusal names the failed receipt, the relevant rerun and its evidence gap, and says when no exact rerun can close it. A failed receipt that any result_submit of this attempt already presented (even a refused one) must be cited again by every later submission, failed outcome included, or it is refused with omitted_failed_check. A mistake in your own bounded standalone python/python3 -c probe (a syntax error, one wrong regex literal or one wrong literal-data expectation) may instead be retracted with checks[].invocation_error bound to the corrected passing run: both receipts stay visible and the failure is retracted, not passed. Runtime verification and actual project test/lint/build failures are never retracted. A mistyped command line whose own output shows the check never started (usage, unrecognized-flag or file-not-found error for the command itself) is not a failed check: do not cite it; cite the corrected command's receipt and describe the mistyped run in the report. The receipt carries node_status (completed or failed), not task acceptance. Top-level write_report-only fields such as artifacts are ignored.

outcome.description: passed: you ran it in this attempt with command_run (or a user-confirmed outside_command) and it exited 0; requires tool_call_ref (see its evidence rule). failed: it ran and failed; always kept as failed, and result_submit refuses an open failure with open_failed_check unless assignment_outcome="failed" intentionally submits a failed assignment. Report a fixed failure that way, or cite only the passing rerun and describe the failure-then-fix history in the report, never by silently dropping it; a different argv needs an explicit supported command_correction (superseded history, never a pass of the original argv). A direct whole-worktree git diff --check whose complete whitespace diagnostics name only sibling writers' reserved paths is runtime-attributed not_attributable, never passed; own writes, unknown paths and runtime verification remain failures. A supported mistake in your own bounded standalone Python probe (see invocation_error.reason) may instead be explicitly retracted with invocation_error; it remains failed history with retracted_by, never passed. A run whose own output shows the check never started because its command line was mistyped (a usage, unrecognized-flag or file-not-found error for the command itself) is not a failed check of the work: do not cite it as one; cite the receipt of the corrected command and describe the mistyped run in the report. Once any result_submit of this attempt cited a failed receipt, even a refused one, every later submission must cite it again (omitted_failed_check otherwise); relabelling it not_run or unverified does not count. A test, lint, type check or build that ran and reported failures is always a real failed check. not_run: a real blocker prevented running it. unverified: it ran but its result could not be established. not_run and unverified require blocker. A passed claim the runtime cannot verify is recorded as unverified with evidence_gap, or as failed when its cited command or a later run of the same command exited nonzero; the result receipt lists each such check.

A project test, lint, type check or build that ran and failed is a real failed check and must never be withdrawn.

A missing, foreign, pending, failed, truncated, replayed or trivial receipt makes a claimed pass unverified or failed, not accepted as passed. Truncated means the retained output, never the 64 KiB inline part (output_truncated), so run a check command directly: a shell script that ends with exit $VARIABLE verifies only in the plain form CHECK; NAME=$?; print/read commands; exit $NAME (evidence_gap status_variable_unproven otherwise). d5e79f7a9024c1bb6ccd0ad27176e94293165801.description: Run one brokered command (argv, no implicit shell) as the owner. Writing workers in Development or Auto get host-writable mounts, an outside cwd and ordinary host resources without routine approval; in Guarded, and for read-only roles in every mode, the host is read-only except tool caches and temp, and writes stay in the granted project scope. Read-only/Guarded commands use private scratch at /var/tmp, not the host directory; a missing path there does not prove host absence. For authorized host-only reads, use an offered outside_command with consent before executing, not a guessed mount or a retry after permission refusal. Read-only investigators cannot use that route: report the capability gap for runtime replanning to a suitable writing specialist, without broadening the requested read. Deletion commands recognized from the argv text (rm, unlink, rmdir, shred -u, find -delete, git clean/rm, rsync --delete, also through common wrappers and sh -c) require consent (Auto answers it itself) and are refused to read-only roles; a deletion inside a script, interpreter or build tool is not recognized. Docker and arbitrary code can bypass direct masks; capability never authorizes hazardous or production actions. Returns argv, exit_code, a tool_call_ref (the evidence a passed result_submit check must cite), output inline up to 64 KiB with output_truncated and the full byte_count, and large_output_id: the complete output is always retained, verifies checks whatever its size and pages with read_large_output, so never redirect or truncate a check's output yourself. Not available to coordinators or consultants.
